papers.title: Mobility-Aware Resource Allocation for mmWave IAB Networks: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
papers.abstract: MmWaves have been envisioned as a promising direction to provide Gbps wireless access. However, they are susceptible to high path losses and blockages, which directional antennas can only partially mitigate. That makes mmWave networks coverage-limited, thus requiring dense deployments. Integrated access and backhaul (IAB) architectures have emerged as a cost-effective solution for network densification. Resource allocation in mmWave IAB networks must face big challenges to cope with heavy temporal dynamics, such as intermittent links caused by user mobility and blockages from moving obstacles. This makes it extremely difficult to find optimal and adaptive solutions. In this article, exploiting the distributed structure of the problem, we propose a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework to optimize user throughput via flow routing and link scheduling in mmWave IAB networks characterized by user mobility and link outages generated by moving obstacles. The proposed approach implicitly captures the environment dynamics, coordinates the interference, and manages the buffer levels of IAB relay nodes. We design different MARL components, considering full-duplex and half-duplex IAB-nodes. In addition, we provide a communication and coordination scheme for RL agents in an online training framework, addressing the feasibility issues of practical systems. Numerical results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Efficient Resource Allocation for On-Demand Mobile-Edge Cloud Computing
papers.abstract: Mobile-edge cloud computing is a new paradigm to provide cloud computing capabilities at the edge of pervasive radio access networks in close proximity to mobile users. Aiming at provisioning flexible on-demand mobile-edge cloud service, in this paper we propose a comprehensive framework consisting of a resource-efficient computation offloading mechanism for users and a joint communication and computation (JCC) resource allocation mechanism for network operator. Specifically, we first study the resource-efficient computation offloading problem for a user, in order to reduce user's resource occupation by determining its optimal communication and computation resource profile with minimum resource occupation and meanwhile satisfying the QoS constraint. We then tackle the critical problem of user admission control for JCC resource allocation, in order to properly select the set of users for resource demand satisfaction. We show the admission control problem is NP-hard, and hence develop an efficient approximation solution of a low complexity by carefully designing the user ranking criteria and rigourously derive its performance guarantee. To prevent the manipulation that some users may untruthfully report their valuations in acquiring mobile-edge cloud service, we further resort to the powerful tool of critical value approach to design truthful pricing scheme for JCC resource allocation. Extensive performance evaluation demonstrates that the proposed schemes can achieve superior performance for on-demand mobile-edge cloud computing.

papers.title: A Survey of Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning with Communication
papers.abstract: Communication is an effective mechanism for coordinating the behaviors of multiple agents, broadening their views of the environment, and to support their collaborations. In the field of multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL), agents can improve the overall learning performance and achieve their objectives by communication. Agents can communicate various types of messages, either to all agents or to specific agent groups, or conditioned on specific constraints. With the growing body of research work in MADRL with communication (Comm-MADRL), there is a lack of a systematic and structural approach to distinguish and classify existing Comm-MADRL approaches. In this paper, we survey recent works in the Comm-MADRL field and consider various aspects of communication that can play a role in designing and developing multi-agent reinforcement learning systems. With these aspects in mind, we propose 9 dimensions along which Comm-MADRL approaches can be analyzed, developed, and compared. By projecting existing works into the multi-dimensional space, we discover interesting trends. We also propose some novel directions for designing future Comm-MADRL systems through exploring possible combinations of the dimensions.

summary: The retrieved literature highlights the application of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) in optimizing resource allocation within cloud computing environments, particularly addressing challenges such as user mobility and dynamic network conditions. While significant advancements have been made in frameworks for resource allocation in both cloud-based deep learning systems and mobile-edge computing, gaps remain in systematic analyses of communication strategies among agents and the adaptability of proposed solutions to real-world complexities. Future research should focus on developing robust, scalable algorithms that can effectively respond to varying user demands and network dynamics.
scholarly_positioning: While prior research has made strides in applying Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) to resource allocation in cloud computing, significant limitations persist, particularly in the systematic analysis of communication strategies among agents and the adaptability of solutions to dynamic environments. Existing frameworks often fail to address the complexities of user mobility and varying Quality of Service (QoS) requirements, leading to suboptimal performance in real-world applications. This proposed research aims to bridge these gaps by developing robust, scalable MARL algorithms that incorporate effective communication mechanisms, thereby enhancing resource allocation strategies in dynamic cloud environments. By situating this work within the broader discourse on adaptive resource management, it seeks to contribute to a more nuanced understanding of MARL's potential in addressing contemporary challenges in cloud computing.
research_scope: This study will investigate the application of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing environments, specifically targeting mobile-edge cloud systems. The research will focus on developing a MARL framework that systematically analyzes communication strategies among agents to enhance coordination and resource allocation efficiency. The evaluation period will span six months, during which the framework's performance will be compared against traditional resource allocation methods in terms of user throughput and Quality of Service (QoS) metrics. Primary outcomes will include the effectiveness of communication strategies in improving resource allocation efficiency, while secondary outcomes will assess the adaptability of the proposed MARL algorithms to varying user demands and network conditions.

technical_feasibility: The proposed study is technically feasible, but it requires access to open-source MARL frameworks for effective implementation and testing. Additionally, GPU resources will be necessary for training the MARL algorithms efficiently. The study does not require human participants or ethics approval, as it focuses on algorithmic performance rather than user interaction. However, if internal representations of agents are analyzed, access to hidden states may be needed. To address potential limitations, the research design should focus on using available open-source MARL libraries and frameworks while ensuring that performance metrics can be evaluated without requiring proprietary data or models.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) in optimizing resource allocation in cloud computing environments, particularly in addressing user mobility and dynamic network conditions; however, they treat communication strategies among agents as secondary or unresolved, leaving unclear whether these strategies significantly affect resource allocation efficiency in real-world applications; this matters theoretically and practically because enhanced communication could lead to improved coordination and performance in dynamic environments; therefore, this study investigates the systematic analysis of communication strategies within MARL frameworks for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing.
question: How do different communication strategies within Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning frameworks impact the efficiency of dynamic resource allocation in mobile-edge cloud computing environments, compared to traditional resource allocation methods, in terms of user throughput and Quality of Service (QoS) metrics?
theoretical_mechanism: In this research, the independent variable is the communication strategies employed within the Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework. The mediator is the coordination efficiency among agents, which is influenced by the effectiveness of these communication strategies. The moderator is the dynamic nature of user demands and network conditions in mobile-edge cloud environments. The dependent variables are the system-level outcomes, specifically resource allocation efficiency, user throughput, and Quality of Service (QoS) metrics. The theoretical framework is grounded in reinforcement learning principles, where enhanced communication leads to improved coordination, thereby optimizing resource allocation. The causal chain posits that better communication strategies enhance coordination, which in turn improves resource allocation efficiency, resulting in higher user throughput and QoS. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the premise that improved communication directly correlates with enhanced coordination and that varying network conditions significantly impact the effectiveness of these strategies.
hypothesis: Implementing advanced communication strategies within Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) frameworks will significantly improve coordination efficiency compared to traditional resource allocation methods, leading to higher user throughput and Quality of Service (QoS) metrics in mobile-edge cloud computing environments.
methodology: This study will implement a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation in mobile-edge cloud computing environments. The procedure involves training multiple agents using various communication strategies, systematically analyzing their impact on coordination efficiency and resource allocation outcomes. Baselines will include traditional resource allocation methods to facilitate comparative analysis. Key operationalized variables include communication strategies (independent variable), coordination efficiency (mediator), and resource allocation efficiency, user throughput, and Quality of Service (QoS) metrics (dependent variables). Evaluation metrics will be derived from system performance logs, focusing on throughput and QoS at the end of each evaluation cycle. To ensure validity, confounding factors such as variability in network conditions and agent learning rates will be controlled through consistent experimental setups. The study aims for reproducibility by utilizing open-source MARL frameworks and publicly available datasets, ensuring that findings can be independently verified.

proposal: This research proposal aims to develop a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for dynamic resource allocation in mobile-edge cloud computing environments, focusing on the systematic analysis of communication strategies among agents and their direct impact on resource allocation efficiency. Key concepts include MARL, dynamic resource allocation, communication strategies, user throughput, and Quality of Service (QoS). The study is technically feasible, leveraging open-source MARL frameworks and requiring GPU resources for algorithm training, while focusing on algorithmic performance without the need for human participants. Positioned within the broader discourse on adaptive resource management, the research seeks to fill the empirical gap highlighted by previous studies, particularly in understanding how communication strategies influence coordination and performance in real-world applications. The primary research question investigates how different communication strategies within MARL frameworks impact resource allocation efficiency, user throughput, and QoS metrics compared to traditional methods. The theoretical mechanism posits that enhanced communication leads to improved coordination among agents, optimizing resource allocation outcomes, with system-level pathways focusing on resource utilization and user-level pathways addressing user experience metrics. The hypothesis is that implementing advanced communication strategies will significantly improve coordination efficiency, resulting in higher user throughput and QoS. Constructs will be operationalized through metrics such as communication protocol efficiency, coordination metrics, and system performance logs, with controlled experimental setups to mitigate confounding factors like network variability. The expected contributions include theoretical advancements in understanding MARL communication dynamics, technical innovations in communication protocols tailored for MARL agents, empirical evidence quantifying the impact of these strategies on user throughput and QoS, and practical deployment guidelines for cloud service providers. Key limitations include potential variability in network conditions and the risk of overfitting to training scenarios, which will be addressed through robust experimental designs and comprehensive reporting of findings.
